key: Every neighbourhood in India has one of
name: ch06_kirana_uncle_names
alt: A kirana-shop uncle behind his counter greets a schoolboy by name while a thought bubble shows the small facts he remembers about the boy's family.
scene: A wide street-level view of a small Indian kirana shop in the evening, shelves behind the counter stacked with biscuit packets, glass jars of sweets and rice sacks. On the LEFT, behind a wooden counter, the shop uncle (about 55, white vest under an open checked half-sleeve shirt, thick moustache, spectacles) leans forward with a warm smile and one hand raised in greeting. A speech bubble from him reads "Arjun beta!". In the CENTRE, a schoolboy (about 12, white shirt, school bag) stands at the counter holding a cloth bag and grinning. Above the uncle floats a large white thought bubble showing the facts he keeps about this one family: a small exam paper with a green tick (the sister's exams), and a biscuit packet with a tag reading "low sugar" (the father's biscuits). A bold label "NAMES" sits at the top of the thought bubble. On the RIGHT, two neighbours, an older lady in a sari and a man holding a newspaper, wait their turn and smile; small dotted lines run from each of them up to tiny name tags in the uncle's bubble area, showing that he holds a little fact for every customer in the colony. A bold label "GOODWILL" sits above the counter on the left. Warm yellow shop light against a dusky blue street, friendly neighbourhood mood.

key: A good family doctor in a small town
name: ch06_doctor_patient_file
alt: A small-town doctor glances at a pencilled note inside a patient's file and asks about the patient's daughter, and the patient beams.
scene: A cosy small-town clinic room seen from the side. On the LEFT, an older family doctor (about 60, grey hair, spectacles, white coat over a cream shirt, stethoscope round his neck) sits at a wooden desk with a thin cardboard file lying open in front of him. A large inset bubble rising from the file shows its inside cover in close-up: pencil lines reading "Ramesh, 52", "daughter in Pune", with a tiny cricket bat and a small sugar cube sketched next to them. A bold label "THE FILE" sits above this inset. The doctor looks up from the file at his patient, mid-question, eyebrows raised kindly; a small speech bubble shows a train and a tiny city skyline, meaning he is asking how Pune is going. On the RIGHT, the patient Ramesh (52, bank clerk, short-sleeved light blue shirt, trousers, small paunch, a pen in his pocket) sits on a stool with his hands on his knees, his face breaking into a surprised, delighted smile. Above Ramesh a bold label reads "REMEMBERED". Background: a calendar on the wall, a shelf of medicine bottles, a window with a tree outside. Soft mid-morning light, calm and warm mood, the whole image centred on the small note that made a big difference.

key: A wedding card arrives from a distant
name: ch06_wedding_card_misspelt
alt: A man holds a beautiful wedding card addressed to Sundeep with the wrong letter circled, while he points it out to his mother.
scene: A home living-room scene in an Indian flat. In the CENTRE FOREGROUND, a large ornate wedding card, deep red with gold borders and a small pair of decorative elephants at the top, is held open in a man's hands; the address line reads "Mr. Sundeep Rao" and the letter u is circled in bright coral with a hand-drawn ring. Beside the card a small paper note shows the correct spelling "Sandeep" with a green tick. A bold label "WRONG NAME" sits above the card. On the LEFT, the man (about 35, kurta, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead) holds the card and turns towards his mother with a slightly hurt, wry half-smile, pointing at the circled letter. On the RIGHT, his mother (about 65, cotton sari, grey bun) sits on a sofa, listening with a patient, amused face, a cup of tea in her hand. A small "2" badge near the man's speech bubble shows that he mentions it to her twice. In the background, a wall calendar with the wedding date circled and a packed suitcase by the door show that he is still going. Soft afternoon light, gentle domestic humour: a kind invitation, and the one small detail that stings.

key: A new joiner from Chennai named
name: ch06_full_name_corridor
alt: Split picture: on day two colleagues shorten a new joiner's long name to Thiru and T; three months later a manager says his full name in the corridor and he smiles.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves inside a modern open-plan office with glass walls and desks. LEFT panel: the new joiner (late 20s, neat moustache, light check shirt, ID lanyard) sits at his desk looking slightly deflated while two colleagues lean over the partition; their speech bubbles read "Thiru" and "T", the second one smaller and careless. A bold label "DAY TWO" sits at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same young man stands in a corridor holding a laptop, and a manager (about 45, grey blazer, spectacles) has stopped him, speaking slowly; a wide speech bubble reads "Thirunavukkarasu" in full, with small dots between syllables to show care. The young man's face breaks into a broad smile and small sparkle lines rise around him; a tiny sun icon near him shows he smiles all afternoon. A bold label "THREE MONTHS" sits at the top of the right panel. Colours: cool greys and teal in the office, warm skin tones, the right half slightly brighter than the left. Mood: from shrinking to standing tall, all because one person took the trouble to say the name properly.

key: A school in a Kerala town needs a new
name: ch06_library_named_father
alt: A headmaster shows a wealthy old student the plan for a school library named after his father, and the old student writes a cheque.
scene: An outdoor scene in front of an old Kerala school building with a sloping red tiled roof, coconut palms and a small garden. In the CENTRE, a new library wing is half built with bamboo scaffolding, and above its door a signboard reads "K. M. Joseph Reading Room". A bold label "HIS FATHER'S NAME" floats above the signboard with a small arrow down to it. On the LEFT, the headmaster (about 58, white mundu and half-sleeve shirt, spectacles, holding a rolled building plan) gestures proudly towards the sign. On the RIGHT, the wealthy old student (about 50, cream kurta, grey at the temples, a slim watch) stands at a small garden table, signing a cheque with a fountain pen, his face soft and moved; a small inset bubble above him shows a faded photograph of an older man with a gentle smile, his father. In the foreground, three schoolchildren in uniform carry library books towards the door, looking up at the sign. A dashed arrow runs from the signboard to the cheque, then from the cheque to the scaffolding, showing name, money, building. Bright morning light after rain, green and hopeful mood.

key: Two chaat stalls on the same street in
name: ch06_chaat_stalls_merge
alt: Two rival chaat stalls on an Indore street; one owner walks over to propose one bigger stall with a board carrying the rival's name, and the rival starts planning.
scene: A street-level evening view of a busy Indian food street with string lights. On the LEFT and RIGHT edges, two small chaat carts stand side by side, each with a tower of pani puri and a price board with a downward red arrow and a coin falling, showing both are selling at a loss. A bold label "PRICE WAR" sits at the top left. In the CENTRE, the first owner (about 40, blue kurta, apron) has walked over from his cart and holds out his open hand, while pointing up with the other hand at a large new signboard drawn above the two carts like a joined roof; the board reads "Sharma-ji's Chaat Corner". The second owner, Sharma-ji (about 50, round face, moustache, orange kurta, ladle in hand), was ready to argue: a fading frown and a crossed-out speech bubble with an angry squiggle sit behind him, and now he points at the empty space between the carts where a dashed outline of a second counter appears. A bold label "HIS NAME" sits beside the new board on the right with an arrow to it. A few customers in the background wait with leaf bowls. Warm golden string-light glow, wry and cheerful mood: pride melted by one name on a board.

key: The night guard at a big Bengaluru tech
name: ch06_night_guard_raju
alt: At night outside a tech park gate, a security guard greets a woman employee by name; she, embarrassed, asks his name, and his badge reads Raju.
scene: A night scene at the glass entrance of a large tech park, tall office blocks with lit windows behind, a boom barrier and a small guard cabin with a desk lamp. On the LEFT, the night guard (about 45, navy security uniform with a cap, moustache, a torch on his belt) stands by the cabin, raising a hand in a friendly goodnight; his speech bubble reads "Good night, Ananya madam". In the CENTRE, a young woman employee (late 20s, kurti and jeans, laptop backpack, ID badge on a lanyard) has stopped mid-step, one hand on her cheek, embarrassed; her small speech bubble shows a question mark. On the RIGHT, a large circular inset bubble shows the guard's name badge in close-up reading "RAJU", with a bold label "HIS NAME" above it. A thin dashed line arcs across the top of the picture showing two years of evenings: a row of small crescent moons passing over the gate. Behind them, a stream of faint grey figures with badges walks out of the building, faceless, showing the two thousand people he sees each day. A bold label "NOTICED" sits above the guard. Deep blue night with warm lamp light around the cabin, quietly touching mood.

key: Walk into almost any temple in South
name: ch06_temple_donor_plaques
alt: A South Indian temple corridor wall covered with small marble donor plaques, one naming who donated the tube lights, while a visitor stops to read it.
scene: An interior view of a stone corridor in a South Indian temple, pillars on the left, a row of tube lights mounted along the top of the wall, and a brass lamp glowing in the distance. The RIGHT two-thirds of the picture is a wall covered with a neat grid of small white marble plaques, each with a few lines of engraved dark text too small to read except one, highlighted with a soft glow, that reads "Tube lights: Sri K. Narayanan". A thin arrow runs from that plaque up to the tube lights overhead, linking the gift and the name. A bold label "DONORS" sits above the plaque wall. On the LEFT, a visitor (about 30, white shirt and veshti, sandal-free bare feet, a small plate of flowers in hand) has stopped walking and leans in to read the glowing plaque, his eyebrows raised with curiosity. Behind him, an older woman in a silk sari also glances at the wall. In the lower right corner, a small inset bubble shows an elderly man smiling proudly as he points at his own name on a plaque, the donor himself. A bold label "YOUR NAME" sits beside the inset. Warm lamp light on stone, calm devotional mood with a hint of gentle humour.

key: A busy cardiac surgeon in Mumbai
name: ch06_surgeon_thanks_nurse
alt: A tired surgeon walking out of an operating theatre stops to thank a junior nurse by name; an inset shows her telling her family that evening.
scene: A hospital corridor just outside an operating theatre with double swing doors and a red light reading "OT" above them. On the LEFT, the cardiac surgeon (about 50, green scrubs, surgical cap, mask pulled down under his chin, tired eyes) has stopped mid-stride on his way out and turns to speak, one hand slightly raised; his speech bubble reads "Thank you, Sister Leena". A wall clock above him shows late evening, and a small stack of files and a ringing phone on a trolley show how busy his day is. In the CENTRE, the junior nurse Leena (about 24, light blue scrubs, cap, an instrument tray in her hands) looks up, surprised and glowing. A bold label "ONE MINUTE" sits above the two of them, with a small stopwatch icon. On the RIGHT, a large inset bubble shows the same evening at home: Leena at a dining table with her parents and younger brother, talking excitedly with her hands while they listen and smile, plates of rice and curry on the table. A bold label "SHE TELLS IT" sits above the inset. A small roster clipboard on the wall near the doors lists names with hers circled, showing how he knew it. Cool hospital light on the left, warm home light in the inset.

key: A good wedding photographer at a big
name: ch06_photographer_learns_names
alt: A wedding photographer directs relatives by name while a three-step strip shows her method: ask the name, repeat it, link it to a detail, and jot it on her phone.
scene: A lively scene at a big Telugu wedding hall with marigold garlands and a decorated stage in the background. On the LEFT, the photographer (about 30, black kurta, camera with a big lens raised, a phone in her back pocket) gestures with one hand as she directs; her speech bubble reads "Ravi garu, a little left". In the CENTRE and RIGHT, three relatives pose in front of the stage: Ravi garu (about 55, white shirt and veshti, big moustache), his brother beside him, and Lakshmi aunty (about 50, bright green silk saree, jasmine in her hair), all smiling as they shuffle into place. Along the bottom of the picture runs a strip of three small panels joined by arrows: first, the photographer asking with a question mark, labelled "ASK"; second, her saying the name back with a small echo symbol, labelled "REPEAT"; third, a tiny green saree and a moustache icon tied with a dotted line to a name tag, labelled "LINK". A small inset of her phone screen above the photographer shows a short notes list with "Lakshmi - green". Bright festive light, gold and green colours, busy but happy mood, the family treating her like one of their own.

key: The canteen anna at your office hands
name: ch06_canteen_anna_murugan
alt: An office worker reads the canteen server's ID card and greets him as Murugan anna; a week later the server adds an extra appalam to his plate.
scene: A split-panel illustration of an office canteen counter with steel food containers, a stack of steel plates and a menu board, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: the canteen server (about 40, white uniform shirt, cap, an ID card on a lanyard, a big ladle in hand) stands behind the counter serving a long queue of plates; a close-up inset of his ID card reads "Murugan". In front, a young office worker (late 20s, striped shirt, office ID badge) smiles and says, in a speech bubble, "Murugan anna, one lemon rice". The server looks up, surprised and pleased. A bold label "BY NAME" sits at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel, a week later (a small calendar icon with an arrow showing seven days): the same server, smiling broadly, places a plate of yellow lemon rice in front of the same worker and adds an extra round appalam with a small curved arrow, while holding out a bowl of sambar; his speech bubble reads "Sambar is good today". A bold label "A WEEK LATER" sits at the top of the right panel. Behind the counter on both sides, a faded queue of other customers shows the hundred plates an hour. Bright midday light, warm and friendly mood.

key: In many Indian families, a grandmother
name: ch06_grandmother_pet_name
alt: In a crowded railway platform a grandmother calls one pet name, and the sound cuts through the crowd to the one grandchild who turns round.
scene: A wide view of a busy Indian railway platform with a train standing on the left, a hanging platform clock, and a crowd of people with suitcases, porters with red shirts carrying luggage on their heads, and a tea vendor with a kettle. The crowd is drawn in muted greys, with small zigzag noise marks floating above it to show the din of announcements and chatter. On the LEFT, a grandmother (about 70, cotton sari, grey hair in a bun, spectacles, one hand cupped beside her mouth) calls out; a bright coral sound wave travels from her mouth in a clean curved line straight through the grey crowd, and a speech bubble near her reads "Chinnu!". On the RIGHT, among three children standing by a pillar, one girl (about 8, yellow frock, two plaits) has turned her head sharply towards the sound with a big smile, while the other two children keep looking elsewhere, unaffected. A bold label "CUTS THROUGH" sits along the top of the sound wave. A small inset bubble in the top right shows three tiny name tags, "Chinnu", "Bablu" and "Pinky", each tied to a different child, showing one pet name per grandchild. A bold label "HER NAME FOR ME" sits under the inset. Warm afternoon light filtering through the platform roof, affectionate mood.
